newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa asks for prayers before foreign trip.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa asks for prayers before foreign trip.

text.p: Mother Teresa said on Thursday as she prepared to leave for Rome that she hoped God would help her through her first foreign trip since she was struck by serious health problems last year.
"I am feeling much better than before...thank God for that," the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun told Reuters by telephone.
She was starting a tour expected to include a meeting with Pope John Paul.
The silver-haired nun was forced to step down as head of her religious order in March as she battled against heart disease.
She said she was planning to head for Poland after Rome.
Asked about her frail health the Nobel Peace laureate said: "God will take care...pray for me."
Earlier, in the eastern city of Calcutta, she told reporters she would also go to the United States if her health allowed.
She will be accompanied by her successor as superior-general of the Missionaries of Charity, Sister Nirmala, four other nuns and her doctor, Patricia Aubanel.
One of the purposes of Mother Teresa's visit to Rome is to formally introduce Sister Nirmala to Pope John Paul.

Sister Nirmala took over as the head of the Calcutta-based Missionaries of Charity when Mother Teresa stepped down after being admitted to hospital three times last year for emergency care and heart surgery.
Aubanel, who was part of the team that carried out Mother Teresa's three heart operations in 1991, 1993 and 1996, said on Wednesday she had advised the nun to visit only Rome.
The nuns, will also be carrying four babies to Europe for adoption, a Missionaries of Charity spokeswoman said.

The spokeswoman said Mother Teresa was scheduled to return by early August. She said the nun was due to attend the initiation ceremony of Missionaries of Charity novices in Rome, but said no date had been fixed for her meeting with the Pope.
Mother Teresa's recent tours outside India have been marred by ill health.

On a visit to Europe in 1993, she injured three ribs in a fall. On a trip to the United States in 1991, she fell ill midway through the visit and had to undergo the first of her three heart operations.
